The R5 endpoint migration moved every `app/api/**/route.ts` in the operator
onto `defineRoute` (mounted on the Hono `app` via `registerAllRoutes`). 243
routes, 24 family batches. A few things that bite if you don't know them:

## Catch-all routes must register LAST

Hono resolves overlapping routes purely by **registration order** — unlike
Next.js file routing, it has **no static-over-dynamic precedence**, so a
parametric/wildcard route (`/:transport`, `/plugins/*`, `/agent-tools/*`)
registered before a literal sibling shadows it outright (the audit's
original finding: `GET /api/marketplace/:slug` registered first 404'd
`GET /api/marketplace/spawnable`).

**Current behavior (2026-07-03): this is now enforced automatically, not by
hand-placement in `ALL_ROUTES`.** `register.ts` classifies every route via
`isCatchAll(path)` (a `*` segment, a greedy `:name{.+}` /`:name{.*}` regex
param, or the exact single-segment `/:transport`) and registers in **two
phases**:

- `registerRouteLiterals(app)` — every non-catch-all route, sorted
  literal-before-param by `bySpecificity()` (a stable sort, so ties keep
  their `ALL_ROUTES` order). Called **before** the composed app mounts its
  sub-apps (`app.route('/harness', …)`, `app.route('/plugins', …)`), so a
  literal `defineTool` always out-ranks a **sub-app's own** parametric/
  catch-all route at the same prefix — the scenario the original hand-ordered
  scheme couldn't reach at all (a sub-app's catch-all lives outside
  `ALL_ROUTES`).
- `registerRouteCatchalls(app)` — the `*` / `:transport` dispatch routes,
  mounted **after** the sub-apps, so a sub-app's real route (e.g. a plugin's
  own `apiRoutes`) still gets first refusal before the projected-tool
  catch-all.

So the position of a route within the `ALL_ROUTES` spread in
`routes/index.ts` is **no longer load-bearing for correctness** — the sort
re-derives literal-before-param order every time regardless of where you
add the import line (the comment markers there are now organizational, not
load-bearing). What IS load-bearing: classifying a genuinely-catch-all route
correctly so `isCatchAll()` sorts it into phase 2, and calling
`registerRouteLiterals` / `registerRouteCatchalls` (not the combined
`registerAllRoutes`) around the real app's sub-app mounts — `registerAllRoutes`
runs both phases back-to-back and is correct only for a bare app with no
sub-apps (the in-process test harness). A regression test —
`__tests__/route-shadowing-invariant.test.ts` — asserts the invariant against
the exact mounted order (`routeRegistrationOrder()`): no parametric route
registers before a literal sibling it would shadow.

## A route module importing the barrel can deadlock the registry

`routes/openapi-json.ts` needs `allRouteFragments()`. Importing it from the
package barrel (`@/lib/endpoint-route`) creates a cycle:
`routes/index.ts → openapi-json.ts → barrel → register.ts → routes/index.ts`.
Import the **leaf module** directly (`../openapi`) instead. Any route module
that needs something from the endpoint-route package must reach for the
specific file, never the barrel.

## Port at the route's *current* auth posture — don't tighten mid-port

Most legacy `route.ts` files were `auth: 'public'` with an inline
`isLoopback()` / `getSessionUser()` / `requirePrincipal()` check. A
mechanical port keeps exactly that: `auth: 'public'` + the same inline
check. Tightening (e.g. making `credentials` require `trust: 'trusted'`) is
a **separate, auditable pass** — never smuggled into a migration diff.
Reviewers can't see a behavior change hidden inside 200 lines of faithful
copy.

## Colocated route.test.ts → Hono in-process app.request()

Old tests imported `{ GET, POST }` from `./route` and called them with a
fake `NextRequest`. The ported test builds a Hono app, `registerAllRoutes`,
and drives `app.request('/api/...')`. Move the file to
`lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/`. Two recurring fixes:

- **Flag-gated routes** (`gateApiRoute(FLAGS.X)`) 404 in tests unless you
  mock the flag gate. Endpoint-route tests now live under
  `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/__tests__/` (moved off the
  `apps/operator` tree with the rest of the barrel — see below), so mock the
  **relative** path, not the old `@/lib/...` Next alias:
  `vi.mock('../../require-flag', () => ({ gateApiRoute: vi.fn(async () => null) }))`.
- **Never `vi.mock('node:fs')`** — `registerAllRoutes` transitively loads
  prompt-assembly, which `existsSync`/`readFileSync`s real persona files. A
  blanket fs mock breaks unrelated routes. Mock the specific lib instead.

## getSessionUser / getSessionUserOrDefault are header-aware

`defineRoute` handlers get a plain `Request`. The Next-free cookie
substrate (`lib/auth.ts`) exposes `getSessionUser(headers?)` /
`getSessionUserOrDefault(headers?)` — pass `req.headers`. The no-arg form
falls back to `next/headers` `cookies()`, which is the thing being removed.

## Enforcement is a script, not a lint rule

`apps/operator/scripts/endpoint-route-progress.mjs --check` exits non-zero
if any raw `route.ts` exists under `app/api/**` outside the
`[[...route]]` host-seam floor. That catches a re-introduced route
regardless of contents — strictly better than a contents-matching ESLint
rule. Wire it into CI next to `tsc`.

Two hardening fixes landed 2026-07-03, both worth knowing if you touch this
script again:

- **A clean checkout with the migration 100% complete has NO `app/api` dir at
  all** (git doesn't materialize a directory with zero tracked files) — the
  script used to shell out to `find "$API" …` unconditionally, and `find` on a
  missing path exits non-zero, which threw out of the wrapping `execSync` and
  crashed the whole script (a false RED on the isolated green-checkpoint
  checkout, which is exactly the fully-migrated end state this script exists
  to celebrate). It now `existsSync(API)`-guards first and treats a missing
  dir as zero remaining routes, not an error.
- **The migrated-count barrel path was relative and silently wrong after the
  barrel moved.** It resolved the `defineRoute` registry barrel as
  `join(API, '../../lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts')` — a path relative to
  `app/api` that broke the moment the barrel moved to
  `packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts` (the
  operator-core extraction), and the `catch` around the read **swallowed the
  error and reported `migratedCount: 0`** instead of surfacing the stale path.
  The barrel is now resolved absolutely from `REPO`
  (`packages/operator-core/lib/endpoint-route/routes/index.ts`), and a failed
  read prints a loud `WARNING` naming the path it tried, rather than quietly
  reporting zero progress. (This only affects the progress *count* the script
  prints — the `--check` non-zero-on-regression enforcement above was never
  affected by the barrel-read failure.)
